[quote=qianxun;60604910][b]Do as I say, not as I do[/b]

The Five Angels would respond to further government regulation with modest criticism, but would nevertheless comply, with the five newly-created political parties registering with the Ascoiyan government. However, Almstedt Corporation would immediately find workarounds to the state's attempt to regulate its banking services. Victoria Strand, president and CEO of Dearborn Bank (Almstedt's premier financial subsidiary) would be chosen to work as the main point of contact by the Chamber with the Ascoiyan government, and would nominally accept the temporary shutdown of financial services while negotiations were underway.

However, while this was going on, Xavier Almstedt would quickly introduce Porthwaite Opportunities into Ascoiya's market. Unlike conventional banking institutions, Porthwaite fell outside the government's parameters, being that rather than a bank it instead operated as a digital wallet. As such, Porthwaite essentially worked as a service for money transfers and payments without providing any of the services typical to banking institutions like deposit services, loans, and interests on savings. While talks were ongoing, Almstedt Corporation would invest heavily in Porthwaite infrastructure, encouraging newly-opened restaurants, convenience stores, and shopping malls to integrate QR codes into its digital ecosystem.

All the while, Almstedt would court the local Ascoiyan banks with corporate partnerships, offering to develop their server infrastructure, computers, websites, mobile apps, to expedite their transition into fully universal banks. Porth Wallet, Porthwaite's mobile app, would be asked to included in any of these dealings so that Ascoiyans can easily transfer funds from their banks to the Porth Wallet. Somare, Qunarco, Miwu Group, and Tencor would follow Almstedt's line and quickly integrate Porthwaite Opportunities into their digital storefronts, thereby offering citizens from all over Ascoiya, near or far, urban or rural, to easily avail of their services by simply depositing money into their Porth Wallets for use in online payments.

It was not just corporate dealings, however. Schools and hospitals in Ascoiya would be flooded with offers to digitize and roboticize. Educational institutions would be projectors and air conditioning units for the classrooms, smartphones and laptops for the students, coffee machines and fridges for faculty. And in the hospitals: telehealth, 3D printing, electronic health records would be proposed to improve patient outcomes and reduce the burden on Ascoiya's healthcare staff. It also made the Chamber of Commerce look good.[/quote]

It was clear the consensus was the same, that the Citizens and common folk would rather stick to their ways than be introduced to the norm of global life, it was something these corporations learned the hard way at least this time that people rejected this idea, or just couldn't wrap their heads around it, some schools on the other hand found it difficult to introduce the offers to digitize into their curriculum, others caught off guard would refuse upon first request, Hospitals though would see the most luck, as many of these took immediate interest although they had their concerns like the rest.

[spoiler=Expansion: Regaining the east (381 words)]
The island of Turnikuz would have a varied and tumultuous history. Initially it would be under the control of the Valdderan first sultanate, along with many other islands in the shamat sea. The Valdderans would use these islands to build a powerful naval presence in the sea. However when the first sultanate collapsed in 1499CE, the Holy Hydronic Empire would capitalise on the opportunity, launching an invasion of Turnikuz, along with Valdderas other colonies in the shamat sea, such as the thalassian islands. The result of the first Hydro-Valdderan war would be a major Hydronian victory. The entirety of the islands in the shamat sea would come under Hydronian possession, being established as two new colonial possessions, Turnikuz and Samzad-Izb. These would complement the already existing imperial colony of Turqevia.

In 1813, Valdderas third sultanate would recognise the Holy Hydronic Empires failing condition and attempt to retake the islands in the second Hydro-Valdderan war. This war would be a Valdderan victory, with them retaking 3 of their former islands. Hydronia would remain in control of the largest island of Turnikuz and three of the islands of Samzad-Izb.

After the Holy Hydronic Empire collapsed in 1822, Turnikuz, Turqevia and Samzad-Izb would be separated from Hydronia forcibly as a result of the treaty of dissolution. They would remain in a state of chaos and statelessness for nearly 100 years, until Hydronia would reclaim the islands in 1908. During this time, the islands would be largely uninhabited, which Hydronia used to justify the reclamation of the land. This would occur during Hydronias reintegration era, when the fragmented states left over from the final war would be reabsorbed into the new federal state. Turnikuz and Turqevia would be reclaimed first, being transformed into a unified federal state of Hydronia, the state of Turqevia. The islands to the east, former parts of Samzad-Izb would be claimed later and also integrated into Turqevia. The islands of Turnikuz, Samzad and Izib Major and Minor would become three constituent sub-state districts in the state of Turqevia; Turnikuz, Samzad and Izib.

Today, the islands boast plentiful ports as well as military bases. These allow trade to continue to flourish in the shamat sea, whilst also allowing Hydronia and Valddera to regulate it, keeping their grip on power in the region.
[/spoiler]
